st: Mix the pork and lamb with the grated onion, [[2 tbsp]] vinegar, [[2 tbsp]] oil, [[2 tsp]] salt and [[1 tsp]] pepper.
Cover and marinate in the fridge for at least 4 hours.
Heat a grill to medium-high with plenty of hot coals or gas flame.
Thread the meat onto skewers, leaving small gaps so it cooks evenly.
Thread the onion wedges, peppers and eggplant on separate skewers and brush with [[1 tbsp]] oil.
Grill the meat for 15 minutes, turning every few minutes, until browned outside and the pork reaches 145°F (63°C).
Grill the vegetables 10 minutes, and the tomato halves 5 minutes, until charred and soft.
Rest the meat for 5 minutes and serve with the vegetables and flatbread.
Rinse the grape leaves in warm water and trim off any hard stems.
Melt [[2 tbsp]] butter in a pan and cook the onion for 6 minutes. Cool for 10 minutes.
Mix the onion with the beef, rice, parsley, dill, [[1 tbsp]] tomato paste, [[1.5 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper.
Lay a leaf shiny side down, put 1 tablespoon of filling near the stem, fold in the sides and roll up snugly.
Line the bottom of a pot with extra leaves. Pack the dolma in tight rows, seam side down.
Pour in [[2 cups]] water and set a heavy plate on top to keep them from unrolling.
Cover and simmer on low for 50 minutes, until the rice is tender and the beef reaches 160°F (71°C).
Mix the yogurt with the garlic.
Serve the dolma warm with the garlic yogurt.
Put the wheat, chicken, onion and [[8 cups]] water in a large heavy pot.
Bring to a boil, skim off any foam, then cover and simmer on low for 90 minutes.
Take out the chicken and check it reached 165°F (74°C). Cool 10 minutes, then shred the meat and discard bones, skin and onion.
Return the meat to the pot with [[2 tsp]] salt.
Cook uncovered over low heat for 60 minutes, stirring every 10 minutes, adding hot water if too dry.
Beat the mixture hard with a wooden spoon or masher until smooth and stretchy.
Stir in [[2 tbsp]] butter and cook 5 minutes.
Spoon into bowls and top with browned butter made from [[2 tbsp]] butter, and cinnamon if you like.
Stir [[1 tsp]] sugar and the yeast into [[1.5 cups]] warm water and let sit for 5 minutes until foamy.
Mix [[4 cups]] flour with [[2 tsp]] salt, then add the yeast water and [[2 tbsp]] oil.
Knead for 8 minutes until smooth and soft.
Cover and let rise for 60 minutes until doubled.
Divide into 8 balls and let them rest 10 minutes under a towel.
Heat the oven to 500°F (260°C) with a baking sheet inside, or heat a dry skillet over high heat.
Roll each ball very thin, into a large oval about 1/8 inch thick.
Bake 1 minute per side in the oven on the hot sheet, or 1 minute per side in the skillet, until puffed with brown spots.
Stack the breads under a towel to keep them soft.

ing: cleaned and split by the butcher
st: Soak the beef feet in cold water for at least 4 hours, changing the water twice, to remove impurities.
Drain, put them in a large pot, cover with water, bring to a boil for 10 minutes, and discard that water. Rinse the feet.
Return the feet to the clean pot with [[16 cups]] fresh water and bring to a gentle boil.
Reduce to a bare simmer and cook with the lid slightly open for 5 hours, skimming now and then, until the meat is tender and falling off the bone.
Add [[2 tbsp]] salt in the last 15 minutes.
Mash the crushed garlic with a pinch of salt and a splash of broth.
Lift out the meat, remove bones and slice or shred it.
Ladle the hot broth and meat into bowls. Add garlic paste to taste.
Serve with torn lavash, sliced radishes and lemon wedges.
Bring [[3 cups]] water to a boil. Add the barley and cook for 30 minutes until tender, then drain.
Whisk the yogurt, egg and [[1 tbsp]] flour in a large pot until completely smooth.
Heat the yogurt mixture over low heat, stirring constantly in one direction, until it just starts to steam. Do not let it boil hard.
Add the cooked barley and [[1 tsp]] salt.
Simmer gently for 10 minutes, stirring often, until slightly thick. The egg must be fully cooked.
Melt [[2 tbsp]] butter in a small pan and cook the onion for 6 minutes until golden, then stir in [[1 tbsp]] dried mint for 30 seconds.
Ladle the soup into bowls and top with the onion-mint butter.
Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Cut a lid from the top of the pumpkin and scoop out the seeds and strings.
Boil [[1 cup]] rice in [[1.5 cups]] water with [[0.5 tsp]] salt for 8 minutes until partly cooked. Drain.
Mix the rice with the apricots, raisins, walnuts, [[1 tsp]] cinnamon, [[2 tbsp]] honey and [[2 tbsp]] melted butter.
Brush the inside of the pumpkin with a little melted butter and fill it with the rice mixture, packing loosely.
Drizzle the remaining honey and butter over the filling and put the lid on.
Set the pumpkin on a baking tray and bake for 75 minutes, until the flesh is soft when poked with a knife.
Check the rice is tender. If not, add a splash of hot water, replace the lid and bake 10 minutes more.
Bring the whole pumpkin to the table, scoop out filling together with some of the soft flesh.
Mix [[3 cups]] flour, the yeast and [[1 tsp]] salt, then add about [[1 cup]] warm water and [[1 tbsp]] olive oil. Knead for 8 minutes.
Cover and let the dough rise for 45 minutes.
Heat the oven to 500°F (260°C) with baking sheets inside.
Mix the beef, tomatoes, onion, bell pepper, parsley, garlic, [[2 tbsp]] tomato paste, paprika, [[1 tsp]] salt and [[2 tbsp]] olive oil.
Divide the dough into 10 balls and roll each into a very thin 7-inch circle.
Spread a thin layer of the meat topping over each circle, right to the edge.
Bake in batches on the hot sheets for 7 minutes, until the edges are crisp and the meat reaches 160°F (71°C).
Serve hot with lemon, fresh herbs and sliced onion, rolled up.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Line a baking sheet with foil.
Pat the trout dry and rub inside and out with [[1 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper.
Mix [[4 tbsp]] soft butter with the juice of 1 lemon.
Stuff each fish with tarragon sprigs, lemon slices and garlic.
Spread the lemon butter all over the outside of the fish.
Place the fish on the sheet and bake for 20 minutes, until the flesh is opaque and flakes easily, 145°F (63°C) inside.
Rest 3 minutes and serve with boiled potatoes and herbs.
Make the filling by mixing [[1 cup]] flour, [[0.5 cup]] melted butter and [[0.5 cup]] sugar into a crumbly paste. Set aside.
Beat [[0.75 cup]] softened butter with [[0.75 cup]] sugar until fluffy, then beat in 1 egg and the vanilla.
Mix [[2.5 cups]] flour with the baking soda, baking powder and salt. Add alternately with the yogurt to the butter mixture to form a soft dough.
Chill the dough for 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C).
Divide the dough in two. Roll one half into a 9-inch round and place on a lined baking sheet.
Spread the filling over it, leaving a small border. Roll the other half to cover, pinching the edges closed.
Score the top in a pattern, brush with a beaten egg, and bake for 35 minutes until golden.
Cool for 20 minutes, then slice into wedges.
Cut out the core of the cabbage and boil the whole head for 10 minutes. Peel off the soft leaves as they loosen.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil and cook the onions for 6 minutes. Cool for 10 minutes.
Mix the onions with the beef, rice, herbs, [[1.5 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper.
Trim thick ribs from the leaves. Put [[2 tbsp]] filling on each leaf, fold in the sides and roll tight.
Line a pot with spare leaves and pack in the rolls seam down.
Mix the tomatoes and [[1 tbsp]] tomato paste with [[2 cups]] water and pour over the rolls.
Cover with a plate to hold them down, cover the pot, and simmer on low for 60 minutes.
Check the filling reaches 160°F (71°C) and the rice is tender. Serve with yogurt.
Put the bulgur in a bowl, pour over the boiling water, cover and leave for 15 minutes until the grains are tender and the water is absorbed.
Add the tomato paste, pepper paste and [[2 tbsp]] olive oil and knead with your hands for 2 minutes, until the bulgur turns a deep orange red and sticks together.
Fold in the scallions, parsley and lemon juice and add salt to taste. This is eech. Press into a dish and chill.
Heat a skillet over medium heat. Add the sujukh slices with [[1 tbsp]] olive oil and fry 3 minutes per side until sizzling, browned and crisp at the edge.
Pull the chechil apart into long strands and arrange on a board with the basturma, tomatoes and tarragon.
Add the warm sujukh and the eech to the board, drizzle with the remaining [[1 tbsp]] olive oil and serve with torn lavash.
nt: Sujukh pan fried in its own fat; bulgur softened in boiling water, no stove needed; the rest is cured or fresh
Best swap: pastrami or other cured beef for basturma; braided mozzarella for chechil.

st: Mix [[2.5 cup]] flour, [[0.75 cup]] water, [[1 tsp]] salt and [[1 tbsp]] oil into a soft dough. Knead 5 minutes and rest, covered, for 30 minutes.
Toss spinach, sorrel, cilantro, dill and scallions with [[1 tsp]] salt in a bowl. Squeeze out the liquid well by hand or the dough will go soggy.
Stir in [[1 tbsp]] oil. Divide the dough into 6 balls.
Roll one ball into a very thin 8 inch round. Spread a thin layer of greens over half, leaving a rim.
Fold the other half over to form a half-moon and press the edge to seal. Repeat with the rest.
Heat a dry skillet over medium-high heat. Cook each half-moon 2 to 3 minutes per side until browned in spots.
Brush with the remaining [[1 tbsp]] oil while hot and serve warm in stacks.
nt: Best swap: kale or Swiss chard, stems removed, replaces the wild greens 1 to 1; add a squeeze of lemon if sorrel is missing.
